verses.1: And Solomon built his house in thirteen years. He completed the construction of his entire house in that time.
verses.2: And he built the house of Lebanon from a hundred meters in length, fifty meters in width. Its height was thirty meters. It stood on four columns made of cypress wood, with cypress branches resting on those columns.
verses.3: And Saphan came down from above, from the branches that were on the pillars. There were forty-five, thirty-five, and eleven pillars in total.
verses.4: And they recite three verses, and move from one verse to another three times.
verses.5: And all the doors and windows were wide open; they moved from one place to another three times.
verses.6: And the pillars themselves were fifty amahs in length, and thirty amahs in width. But on their surfaces, they were thick.
verses.7: But the throne where judgment will be carried out… But the judgment was carried out, and it ended with branches from the ground reaching up to the sky.
verses.8: And in his house, where he lived, there was a courtyard next to the house of Loelem. This was done as a gift for Pharaoh’s daughter, who was taken away by Solomon, just as it was planned.
verses.9: All these stones are very valuable, like precious gems. They’re found in various places: inside and outside the house, as well as in the offices and beyond. They’re also found outside the large courtyard.
verses.10: And precious stones were laid down there. There were very large stones; twelve cubits in size, and also stones weighing a full amah.
verses.11: And from the top of those precious stones, there are magnificent crystals and opal.
verses.12: And the large courtyard was surrounded by three huge towers, as well as towers made of cypress trees. There was also a house of God inside that courtyard.
verses.13: And King Solomon sent for Hiram from Zor.
verses.14: This son of a woman from Almanya was the son of Naphtali. His father was a man from Zorah who was skilled in magic. He possessed wisdom, intelligence, and the ability to carry out any task using magic. He went before King Solomon and did all his tasks.
verses.15: And he created the two pillars. The distance between one pillar and the other was twelve meters. The second pillar was also twelve meters in length.
verses.16: And he made two covers for the heads of those who were to be sacrificed. The first cover was five amots in length, and the second cover was also five amots in length.
verses.17: “Shvakim” refers to actions that lead to growth. It also refers to the actions taken to strengthen the roots of those who are on the heads of the idols. There are seven such actions related to the first idol, and seven actions related to the second idol.
verses.18: And he made the inscriptions and two columns around the altar, so that they could cover the crowns that were on the heads of the priests. He also made the second crown in the same manner.
verses.19: And the crowns that are on the heads of the statues are made by Shushan. But they cost four amos each.
verses.20: And there are also seals on both of those tablets. They are also located above the edges of the tablets themselves. Around these seals, there are various decorations.
verses.21: And he made the idols for the gods. He also made the Canaanite idol and called its name “Yachin”. Then he made the Semitic idol and called its name “Boez”.
verses.22: And on top of the pillars, there was a structure made of wood; it served as a support for the pillars.
verses.23: And he made the sea divide into twelve parts from one side of it to the other. He also made five parts around it. And he divided it into thirty parts around its circumference.
verses.24: And they are released from beneath his lips. Around him, there are twelve ships that navigate the sea. Two ships are set in motion by those who have been released.
verses.25: It stands on twelve bases, with three sides facing north and east, and three sides facing south and west. The sea is above it, and all its surroundings are covered with water.
verses.26: And Abiyu stepped forward, and his lips moved as if they were those of a flower that bloomed in thousands of petals.
verses.27: And he made the columns: twelve in number, with each column being four cubits in length, four cubits in width, and three cubits in height.
verses.28: And this is the act of construction from their edges, and from the edges between the layers.
verses.29: And on the seams between the layers of fabric, there are also seams for joining the upper and lower parts of the fabric together. These seams are made by sewing from above and below the layers of fabric.
verses.30: And four of the nails for the one tent, and four of the nails for the other tent. Their heads were like hats, placed beneath the corners of the hats. They were inserted through each other from person to person.
verses.31: And its mouth is from the inside of the “Koteret” and rises upward. Its lips are curved in a certain way. Half of its mouth is also covered with decorations and ornaments. They’re not curved at all.
verses.32: And the four wings are located below the doors. The position of each wing is one arm’s length and half an arm’s length.
verses.33: And the actions of those who are Ophans are similar to those of those who ride horses. Their hands, their backs, their limbs, and all their body parts are covered with scales.
verses.34: And four of its wings correspond to the four sides of the structure.
verses.35: And at the top of the pole, there was a half-angel standing there. Her hands and feet were tied to the pole.
verses.36: And they opened their doors and their windows, with huge stones and boulders in place of them. It was like a city wall around it.
verses.37: That is how he made the twelve columns. Each column was of one size and one thickness.
verses.38: And he made twelve pillars of copper. Forty daughters of Yachil were involved in this work. Each pillar was four cubits long. Each pillar was one unit in length, and these pillars served to support the twelve columns that were needed for the construction.
verses.39: And he set up five poles on the right side of the house. Five other poles were set up on the left side of the house. The sea was also placed on the east side of the house, above the north side.
verses.40: And Hiram did all the work related to the doors, the windows, and the other decorations. Hiram was able to carry out all the tasks that Solomon had ordered for the Temple of Jehovah.
verses.41: There are two handles and two flaps that cover the two handles on top of the statues.
verses.42: And the rims are four hands wide, for each of the two handles. These two rims serve to cover the two edges of the decorations that are located on the front of the symbols.
verses.43: And there were twelve columns, and there were also twelve arches on those columns.
verses.44: And the one sea, and the two dozen days under that sea.
verses.45: And these vessels, and these utensils, and all these items that Hiram made for King Solomon in the House of God… Nekho’s workmanship was excellent.
verses.46: In the valley of Yarden, the king dug up the land, between the hills and the rivers.
verses.47: And Solomon distributed all the food in great abundance, so much that it could not be measured by any scale.
verses.48: And Solomon did all the utensils that the House of God needed for the golden altar and the altar on which the bread of Presence was placed.
verses.49: And the lamps were five on the right side, and five on the left side, in front of the altar. They were all made of gold.
verses.50: And the doors, and the windows, and the shelves, and the pedestals, all made of gold. They were used to seal the doors of the inner room, which was dedicated to the Holy Things. These doors served as entrances to the golden hall.
verses.51: And all the work that King Solomon did in the Temple of God was completed. Then Solomon brought the treasures of David his father, along with gold and silver, and all the other offerings that were to be given to the Temple of God.
